mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact leaves PermMatrix.Allowed unconstrained, allowing any role-operation pairs. The LeastPrivilege and role-specific assertions will fail because denied operations become allowed.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { Customer -> ClaimApplication in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows applications to have missing or duplicate audit entries. The assertion will find instances where an application transitioned without a corresponding event.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some app: LoanApplication | app.status = UnderReview and no e: ApplicationEvent | e.application = app and e.previous_status = Submitted and e.new_status = UnderReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a non-assigned officer to decide an application. The assertion will find a counterexample where a decided application was decided by someone other than the assigned officer.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_FR_013_Violation { some app: LoanApplication, officer: User | app.status = Approved and officer != app.assigned_officer and officer.role = LoanOfficer and (some d: Decision | d.application = app and d.decided_by = officer) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a customer to have multiple concurrent in-flight applications. The assertion will find a customer with two applications both in Submitted or UnderReview status.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_FR_008_Violation { some disj app1, app2: LoanApplication, customer: User | customer.role = Customer and app1.customer = customer and app2.customer = customer and (app1.status = Submitted or app1.status = UnderReview) and (app2.status = Submitted or app2.status = UnderReview) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows an application in UnderReview (or beyond) to have no assigned officer or an assigned officer who is not a loan officer. The assertion will find a counterexample where concurrency race was not properly resolved.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ConcurrencySafetyViolation { some app: LoanApplication | app.status = UnderReview and app.assigned_officer = none }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to be created by the wrong actor (e.g., a claim event not by a loan officer). The assertion will find instances where audit-entry attribution does not match the transition type.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionCorrectnessViolation { some e: ApplicationEvent, c: User | c.role = Customer and e.previous_status = Submitted and e.new_status = UnderReview and e.actor = c }
